title: Snapshots, replay and deterministic recovery

objectives.text: Bind a coherent snapshot to exact schema/session and a documented inclusive/exclusive cursor, recovering only through a validated contiguous target before publishing current state.
Demonstrate full replay equals snapshot-plus-suffix under the same reducer/configuration while isolating external effects and retaining source/version/provenance and failure limits.

blocks.markdown: A snapshot must pair application state with the exact stream position it represents, plus schema/reducer version, configured session/channel, instrument directory and relevant rules/configuration. State from after event100 with a cursor from before100 can double-apply or omit work. A checksum of that inconsistent artifact does not make it coherent. Capture/publish state and cursor under one consistent cut or equivalent transactional/versioned protocol. Validate schema/ranges/source and completeness, but remember that shape checks alone cannot prove the snapshot came from a trusted coherent source.

Choose an explicit convention. Our toy snapshot field through means LAST APPLIED event inclusive, so replay begins through+1. That is an OWN convention, not a rule to impose on every protocol. The Nasdaq GLIMPSE5 End of Snapshot G message specifies that real-time ITCH processing begins WITH the sequence number stated in its snapshot message, not blindly that number+1. GLIMPSE also has its own SoupBinTCP snapshot sequence separate from the real-time feed cursor. Read the exact protocol/service cursor meaning and bind the same session/day/feed before joining snapshot and updates.

blocks.title: A complete suffix must meet one coherent cut

steps.text: Toy initial A=10,B=10 through0. Apply1:A+2 ->(12,10),2:B-3 ->(12,7),3:A-1 ->(11,7). Next expected after these events is4.
A coherent snapshot through2 contains(12,7). Replay only event3 to target-next4 and obtain(11,7),the same as replaying all three from through0.

If(12,7)is paired with through1, replaying2 again double-applies B-3. If it is paired with through3, event3 is omitted. Ranges/checksum might still look valid; coherent capture/source evidence is essential.

blocks.caption: Expected lines: (4, (11, 7)); True; noncontiguous replay; (1, 'DAY1', 0, (10, 10)). Schema1/sessionDAY1,<=16 delta events,two exact integer counts0..100 and delta -10..10 are own finite model bounds. Input is immutable snapshot tuples plus caller-owned list; candidate state stays local and is returned only at the exact target. No partial result on failure. This does NOT authenticate snapshot provenance, repair a mixed cursor/state, persist anything or provide atomic publication to concurrent readers.

blocks.markdown: A safe workflow keeps consumers paused, obtains a source-bound complete snapshot and required contiguous suffix, builds a private candidate, validates target/invariants and publishes state/cursor/availability together only after success. Buffer or request updates under an explicit bounded retention/overflow policy while snapshot capture runs; a dropped suffix requires starting recovery again, not hiding the gap. Keep the previous state labeled stale until the replacement is accepted. End-of-snapshot/end-of-session or a heartbeat is not itself proof our own suffix is complete. This lesson returns a pure candidate; concurrent atomic publication and durable recovery are later implementation work.

Deterministic replay requires the same ordered normalized events, reducer/schema version, initial snapshot and rule configuration. Capture historical reference data/FX/fees/calendar decisions that affect results instead of querying today's values during a replay. Avoid implicit wall clocks, unrecorded randomness and unstable iteration-dependent ties in the reducer. Exact integers here make equal event sequences produce exact equal count states; floating reductions or parallel order need explicit tolerance/order policy elsewhere. A source hash/config manifest records what was used; it is not an authenticated source or correctness proof by itself.

Replaying historical fills/orders for a local state rebuild must not resend old orders,cancels,payments,emails or other external mutations. Isolate reducers/projections from effect execution and define idempotency/transaction boundaries for genuinely new effects separately. An append-only log or a duplicate map alone does not atomically commit an external action and its processed marker. Disk write/close alone is not a durable coherent checkpoint. The pure functions here intentionally make no live-service/file/account calls.

Independent transfer: generate a valid bounded event log and compute every prefix state. For each cut, form a snapshot from that SAME prefix and replay the exact suffix to a common target; compare with full replay. Test through0,empty suffix at the target,last valid sequence,wrong session/schema,duplicate/out-of-order/gap,invalid count delta and early/late target. Demonstrate a mixed state/cursor that passes field validation but yields the wrong candidate, then explain why provenance/capture evidence cannot be replaced by a pure shape validator.

Sources: [Nasdaq GLIMPSE5 cursor semantics](https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/content/technicalsupport/specifications/dataproducts/NQGlimpseSpecification_5.0.pdf), [MoldUDP64 session/request definitions](https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/content/technicalSupport/specifications/dataproducts/moldudp64.pdf), [Fowler event-sourcing snapshot/replay/external interaction discussion](https://martinfowler.com/eaaDev/EventSourcing.html), and [Azure event-sourcing tradeoffs/versioning/concurrency](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/event-sourcing). Fowler is a2005 draft conceptual source,not a current vendor recovery contract. The toy cursor/count rules are own explicit model,not a Nasdaq snapshot implementation.

summary: A snapshot is state plus a coherent source/session/version/cursor contract. Build and validate a contiguous candidate to the intended target before resuming; preserve exact replay inputs and suppress historical external effects. Pure deterministic equality does not prove authenticated capture,durable commit or concurrent publication.
